column.text: Bitcoin is testing the critical $78,000 support level as institutional ETF outflows of $120 million today contrast sharply with a seven-day net inflow of $820 million. This divergence signals active profit-taking and rotation rather than a fundamental breakdown, yet the immediate pressure remains heavy. The market bias has shifted neutral-to-bearish because long liquidations totaling $41.3 million vastly outnumber short liquidations at just $13.3 million, confirming that the current downtrend is fueled by forced selling cascades. While stablecoin dry powder remains high and suggests potential for a sharp relief rally if shorts are eventually squeezed, the dominant risk is the continuation of the -3.31% daily drawdown which invalidates the $76,000 hold level and triggers further deleveraging. The decoupling of crypto from the Nasdaq with a correlation coefficient of only 0.18 highlights that this move is liquidity-driven rather than macro-correlated. Dollar liquidity is contracting as risk assets push into a headwind, so traders should demand more proof on continuation longs and treat failed rallies as better-odds shorts. Avoid the mid-zone where risk-to-reward ratios bleed between two and four; instead, favor mean reversion at range extremes with conservative sizing. The tape remains mixed with no directional tailwind either way, requiring a clean mechanism in either direction. Even with headlines of Visa and Mastercard joining forces on AI agent payments or Solana ecosystem tokens rallying above $180 million in market cap, the structural weakness persists until deleveraging subsides. Do not chase breakouts without a real catalyst, as the floor has been breached and volatility will likely expand before any sustained recovery.
